Definition: neuter of G4707 as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly:--very diligently.
BiblicalUsage: The word is the comparative, more diligent: the brother Paul sends was oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence Paul has in the Corinthians.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the more diligent brother shows that faithfulness grows, and a tested man is the one to trust with the offering.
